cases.name: mysql_aggregate_alias_collision
cases.reason: Uses aggregate aliases in HAVING and ORDER BY while deliberately reusing the physical column name Name as an output alias; grouped and joined columns remain reads.
cases.sql: SELECT g.Name AS genre_name, COUNT(t.TrackId) AS track_count, SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS Name FROM Genre AS g LEFT JOIN Track AS t ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId GROUP BY g.Name HAVING track_count > 0 ORDER BY Name DESC

cases.name: mysql_aggregate_aliases
cases.reason: Groups invoice counts and revenue by country and reuses both aggregate aliases in HAVING and ORDER BY.
cases.sql: SELECT c.Country AS country, COUNT(i.InvoiceId) AS invoice_count, SUM(i.Total) AS revenue FROM Customer AS c JOIN Invoice AS i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.Country HAVING revenue > 0 ORDER BY revenue DESC, invoice_count DESC

cases.name: mysql_case_if_ifnull
cases.reason: Builds customer labels with IFNULL and CONCAT, classifies countries with IF and support assignment with CASE, and filters on email presence.
cases.sql: SELECT c.CustomerId AS customer_id, IFNULL(c.Company, CONCAT(c.FirstName, ' ', c.LastName)) AS display_name, IF(c.Country = 'USA', 'domestic', 'foreign') AS market, CASE WHEN c.SupportRepId IS NULL THEN 'unassigned' ELSE 'assigned' END AS support_status FROM Customer AS c WHERE c.Email IS NOT NULL ORDER BY display_name

cases.name: mysql_casefold_backticks
cases.reason: References a PascalCase table and columns with backticks and deliberately varied column case; MySQL and MariaDB resolve those column identifiers case-insensitively.
cases.sql: SELECT `trackid` AS track_id, `NAME` AS track_name FROM `Track` WHERE `UNITPRICE` >= 0.99 ORDER BY `NAME`

cases.name: mysql_casefold_alias
cases.reason: Uses mixed-case quoted output aliases and refers to one alias with different case in ORDER BY, exercising case-insensitive alias lookup while preserving the declared output names.
cases.sql: SELECT t.TrackId AS `Track_ID`, t.Name AS `Track_Name` FROM `Track` AS t ORDER BY `track_id`

cases.name: mysql_correlated_invoice
cases.reason: Combines a correlated scalar maximum with a correlated EXISTS filter; the outer customer key and both invoice predicate/value columns remain dependencies.
cases.sql: SELECT c.CustomerId AS customer_id, (SELECT MAX(i.Total) FROM Invoice AS i WHERE i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId) AS max_invoice_total FROM Customer AS c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Invoice AS i2 WHERE i2.CustomerId = c.CustomerId AND i2.Total >= 20) ORDER BY max_invoice_total DESC

cases.name: mysql_cte_alias_chain
cases.reason: Carries line values through two CTE scopes before joining invoice totals back to invoice headers; CTE join and filter aliases remain reads.
cases.sql: WITH line_values AS (SELECT il.InvoiceId AS invoice_id, il.Quantity * il.UnitPrice AS amount FROM InvoiceLine AS il), totals AS (SELECT invoice_id, SUM(amount) AS total_amount FROM line_values GROUP BY invoice_id) SELECT i.InvoiceId AS invoice_id, totals.total_amount AS total_amount FROM Invoice AS i JOIN totals ON totals.invoice_id = i.InvoiceId WHERE totals.total_amount > 0 ORDER BY total_amount DESC

cases.name: mysql_derived_alias_star
cases.reason: Expands a derived-table wildcard using its output aliases, keeping the aliases as view columns and retaining the inner filter dependency.
cases.sql: SELECT report.* FROM (SELECT InvoiceId AS sale_id, Total AS amount FROM Invoice WHERE Total > 0) AS report ORDER BY report.amount DESC

cases.name: mysql_except_lineage
cases.reason: Subtracts customers that have invoices; the right branch contributes membership reads while EXCEPT output values retain only the left branch source.
cases.sql: SELECT c.CustomerId AS customer_id FROM Customer AS c EXCEPT SELECT i.CustomerId FROM Invoice AS i

cases.name: mysql_group_concat_order
cases.reason: Concatenates album tracks in TrackId order; both the concatenated names and ordering keys influence the output while HAVING keeps the count input as a read.
cases.sql: SELECT a.AlbumId AS album_id, GROUP_CONCAT(t.Name ORDER BY t.TrackId SEPARATOR '; ') AS track_names FROM Album AS a LEFT JOIN Track AS t ON t.AlbumId = a.AlbumId GROUP BY a.AlbumId HAVING COUNT(t.TrackId) > 0 ORDER BY album_id

cases.name: mysql_intersect_lineage
cases.reason: Intersects genre-selected tracks with playlist membership, so both branches contribute output value sources and the genre predicate remains a read.
cases.sql: SELECT t.TrackId AS track_id FROM Track AS t WHERE t.GenreId IN (1, 3, 13) INTERSECT SELECT pt.TrackId AS track_id FROM PlaylistTrack AS pt

cases.name: mysql_natural_left_star
cases.reason: Expands the preserved Invoice side of a NATURAL LEFT JOIN; the merged CustomerId remains a read from both relations while the wildcard values come from Invoice.
cases.sql: SELECT i.* FROM Invoice AS i NATURAL LEFT JOIN Customer AS c WHERE i.Total > 0 ORDER BY i.InvoiceId

cases.name: mysql_named_window_frame
cases.reason: Resolves named partition/order windows for row numbering and a framed running average; ranking has no frame because MariaDB rejects it, and partition/order expressions are value sources for each output.
cases.sql: SELECT t.TrackId AS track_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER genre_rank AS genre_position, AVG(t.UnitPrice) OVER genre_window AS running_price FROM Track AS t WINDOW genre_rank AS (PARTITION BY t.GenreId ORDER BY t.Milliseconds DESC), genre_window AS (PARTITION BY t.GenreId ORDER BY t.Milliseconds DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)

cases.name: mysql_right_using_key
cases.reason: RIGHT JOIN USING preserves the Customer key on the right side; both key columns remain join reads and the email filter is a read-only dependency.
cases.sql: SELECT CustomerId AS customer_id, c.Email AS email FROM Invoice AS i RIGHT JOIN Customer AS c USING (CustomerId) WHERE c.Email IS NOT NULL ORDER BY customer_id

cases.name: mysql_union_lineage
cases.reason: Unions playlist membership with invoice lines meeting a quantity threshold, preserving both branch sources for the shared track_id output.
cases.sql: SELECT pt.TrackId AS track_id FROM PlaylistTrack AS pt UNION SELECT il.TrackId AS track_id FROM InvoiceLine AS il WHERE il.Quantity > 1

cases.name: mysql_window_frame
cases.reason: Computes a three-row rolling duration per genre, so the window partition and order columns contribute to output lineage while the price predicate remains a read.
cases.sql: SELECT t.TrackId AS track_id, t.Name AS track_name, SUM(t.Milliseconds) OVER (PARTITION BY t.GenreId ORDER BY t.TrackId ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS rolling_ms FROM Track AS t WHERE t.UnitPrice >= 0.99 ORDER BY track_id
